I think I just pointed out my first QM, though. Hope that's okay. All comments are welcome and appreciated. Thank you advance.

Your marked S/D zones look good, although all of them aren't marked. I don't expect you wanted to do that though otherwise it'd be quite busy. As for the compression zones, good for the most part. A couple, esp. the one farthest to the top, have some s/d pockets that are still prominently sticking out so I would be careful with that. I always take a horizontal line and kind of "scan" the entire zone to make sure all or the vast majority of pockets have been consumed, usually by the wicks of the next candles. The QM looks valid but that's not my area of expertise quite yet.

What in your opinion is a "failed RBD"???
Hi Pivo, Failed RBD is which didn't hold. When price returned back it got ignored and new RBD formed.

PivO wrote: What in your opinion is a "failed RBD"???

An RBD implies the presence of supply. When price comes back to the RBD we might expect a bearish reaction. If however price rallies past the RBD then one might assume that supply was ignored. However it would be interesting to know what price did futher to the left of this "failed RBD".

Hi fxpundit I think this is just a terminology problem. I found the terms a little confusing at first.. I think A RBD or DBR just is - it doesn't fail or succeed. It is simply a turning point/ price cap. Price can fail to return to any of these levels - FTR. I'm no expert, but have just been through the same process of making sense of the terms in use here.
